# MARVIN SIGNATURE ULTIMATE DH CONFIGURATION - UPDATED FINDINGS DOCUMENT
## Research Update: March 16, 2026

## 1. PRODUCT OVERVIEW

**Manufacturer:** 
Marvin Windows and Doors (Warroad, Minnesota, USA)


**Material Class:** 
Wood interior with aluminum-clad exterior


**Configuration Type:** DH (Double Hung)

**Country of Origin:** United States

**Product Line Position:** 
The Marvin Ultimate collection is indeed the ultimate in window and door design, offering colors, sizes, shapes, and materials for virtually any need.
 
The Marvin Ultimate Collection is Marvin's most customizable line of windows and doors. It features natural wood interiors, premium exterior options, and extensive design flexibility, making it ideal for custom homes, architectural projects, and builds that require large sizes or distinctive detailing.


## 2. CONFIRMED FINDINGS

### Performance Specifications

**U-Factor:** The Marvin Ultimate double-hung window has a U-factor ranging from 0.25-0.48 (Southwest Exteriors, December 2024). However, 
You will need to call Marvin's architectural department to get the actual test data/report to see the specific number.


**SHGC (Solar Heat Gain Coefficient):** The Marvin Ultimate double-hung window has an SHGC of 0.18-0.52 (Southwest Exteriors, December 2024).

**Visible Transmittance (VT):** The Marvin Ultimate double-hung window has a visible transmittance of 0.39-0.59 (Southwest Exteriors, December 2024).

**Air Infiltration:** 
Marvin says their casement windows have less than 0.01 cfm/ft2 air leakage for their casement windows in the Ultimate series
. However, specific data for DH configuration is not published by Marvin.

### Construction Specifications

**Frame Material:** 
Marvin Ultimate windows and doors feature natural wood interiors that are meticulously selected and crafted for exceptional quality and visual warmth. Each component is carefully vetted to ensure a refined finish and lasting beauty that elevates the character of your home.
 
Marvin Ultimate products feature carefully selected natural wood interiors paired with durable exterior options, including extruded aluminum cladding or wood exteriors.


**Exterior Cladding:** 
Made with the industry's highest level of certification, AAMA 2605, extruded aluminum and backed by a 20-year warranty against chalking and fading.


**Spacer System:** Based on baseline research, marvin uses cardinal glass with a stainless steel spacer. marvin uses a true stainless steel spacer, its more of a "V shape" opposed to ppg's u-shaped. its also a true duel seal.

**Seal System:** Confirmed dual seal system through baseline research findings.

### Size and Configuration Options

**Size Range:** 
Up to 5' wide by 10' tall


**Functionality:** 
Allows easy access to the exterior glass for cleaning and maintenance


### Certification and Standards

**AAMA 2605 Certification:** 
Marvin Ultimate has a wood core composition and features an aluminum-clad exterior that passes the American Architectural Manufacturers' Association (AAMA 2605) standard certification, making the window products resistant to chalk and erosion.


**ENERGY STAR Status:** 
Meet ENERGY STAR standards in energy efficiency with multiple glass options for various regions & climates


**2025 Federal Tax Credit Status:** While Marvin does not participate in the 2025 federal tax credit program, many customers may still qualify for local rebates. You can check for available programs using the ENERGY STAR® Rebate Finder. Marvin encourages customers to review these opportunities, though rebate availability varies by location and is not guaranteed.

**Coastal Certification:** 
SUPERIOR WEATHER PERFORMANCE: The window's performance ratings are best in class, including an IZ3 certified coastal options


**Design Pressure Rating:** 
Superior performance: Top-class performance ratings, including DP50 on most sizes, along with IZ3 certified coastal options, offer greater peace of mind in severe weather.


### Warranty Terms

**Coverage Structure:** Based on baseline research, This Limited Warranty extends to the owner of the structure in which the products are originally installed and is fully transferable

**Glass Coverage:** Based on baseline research, glass is warranted for 20 years in sizes up to 60 square feet and 10 years for sizes over 60 square feet.

**Hardware and Non-Glass Components:** Based on baseline research, hardware and non-glass components are warranted for 10 years.

**Exterior Finish:** 
For the exterior finish, Marvin Ultimate provides 20 years. The warranty covers manufacturing defects resulting in chalk, fade, and loss of adhesion (peel).


**Interior Finish:** For the interior finish, Marvin Ultimate offer 5 years of warranty, which covers the stained or painted interior finish defects, including peeling, delamination, checking, cracking, blistering, and flaking. It also covers excessive chalking, fading, or changing in color under normal interior environmental conditions.

**Transferability:** Marvin offers a fully transferable, limited warranty

## 4. RED FINDINGS

**Recent Quality Control Issues (2024):** 
The quality is atrocious. The interior paint is incomplete in many areas. In others, there's debris in the dried paint and large dried drip areas. The exterior clad is defective and not powder coated with exterior color, so it looks silver
 (Houzz Forum, 2024) - INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW (manufacturing defect).

**Hardware Reliability Issues:** 
I have Ultimate Casement windows. These are Marvin's top-of-the-line. The handles break off frequently.
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW (hardware defect).

**Structural Issues:** 
My Marvin ultimate windows are 19 months old. I opened a few windows that I've never opened and found that the corners are completely separated.
 (GBA Forum, 2023) - INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM (unclear if installation or product defect).

**Service Response Issues:** The technician never shows up. The technician just sends parts in the mail and then tells you to install them yourself. These technicians are 3rd party and just scam Marvin and the user.

**Manufacturing Quality Issues:** I recently purchased 27 Marvin Ultimate Next Generation windows and could not be more dissatisfied. The windows are very flimsy, the double hung windows do not operate as advertised, very cheaply constructed with finger-jointed scrap wood!! (OldHouseGuy.com, October 2024) - INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW (product defect).

**Long-term Durability Concerns:** 
I have had to replace at least 10 windows with two more now due to rot. I contacted Marvin but no help. I would not recommend these windows unless you plan to replace all in 15 to 20 years
 (TheWindowDog.com, 2024) - INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW (product longevity issue).

**Parts Availability Issues:** 
Marvin won't sell you any parts (and these are simple parts). Marvin gave me four different dealers - all lumber yards - that sell Marvin windows.
 Multiple dealers provided poor service for parts requests (Houzz Forum, 2024).

## 5. YELLOW FINDINGS

**Performance Data Transparency:** Critical NFRC-certified performance values for Ultimate DH configuration are not published as specific values, requiring direct manufacturer contact for detailed specifications.

**Installation Complexity Concerns:** 
I'm in full agreement with Armando (post #4) regarding the corner gaskets on the "fold out" flange windows. I was less than impressed with these gaskets and used my own made from Siga tape
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: HIGH.

**Spacer System Performance:** Based on baseline research, Cardinal does call their XL (stainless steel) a warm edge spacer, but the energy performance still "trails" super spacer by about 4 to 6 degrees depending on a warm side or cold side measurement.

**Field Installation Issues:** 
I believe the windows are great, but the flanges around some of their windows are cut out at the corners to facilitate shipping. The result is that they send some foamy corner gaskets with a sticky back to be glued in place, but half of the time those gaskets get lost, forgotten to be installed or put in place on dirty flange and/or sheathing, therefore, the chance for moisture problems increases a lot
.

## 9. SPECIALTY FORUM FINDINGS

If you go Marvin, they do have a triple paned option. If you go with that and install mostly casements, you'll be making some reasonably good choices regarding thermal performance and air infiltration without getting into the weeds


- **Material Confirmation:** 
I believe that the Ultimate series has an aluminum clad exterior, or at least the ones that I just installed did


- **Installation Experience:** 
Installed Marvin Ultimate G2 (aluminum clad) in 2x6 wall and had no issues with condensation last winter


- **Installation Concerns:** 
I'm in full agreement with Armando (post #4) regarding the corner gaskets on the "fold out" flange windows. I was less than impressed with these gaskets and used my own made from Siga tape

As well, Marvin's reputation for service is generally well respected.

- **Cost Comparison:** 
To upgrade to those, the price per slider jumps from a 2020 quote of $2198 each to $22,000 each for the Marvin Ultimate, so I will not be doing that.
